page: Microsoft Azure D64ns_v6 belongs to the general-purpose Dnv6 virtual machine series, hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores at 4.2 GHz, powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor. Memory capacity is 256.0 GB, establishing a standard 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The hardware architecture incorporates 260 MB of L3 cache and supports specialized instruction extensions including AVX-512, Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX for tile and INT8 math), and hardware cryptographic routines such as VAES and SHA-NI. The instance is diskless, containing no integrated local storage, and does not include GPU acceleration.

Benchmark data reflects strong computing and networking metrics. In PassMark evaluations, the instance recorded a CPU score of 67,051.45, with strong performance in extended instructions (71,083.39) and cryptographic workloads (56,353.15). Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieved 347.46 GB/sec. Synthetic memory tests revealed 4,125.39 GB/sec in small-block cached reads, although large-block uncached bandwidth and overall PassMark memory scores ranked lower. Network-bound throughput reached top-tier levels with 90.06 GB/sec in static web serving and 71.06 million operations per second in Redis SET testing. Intel AMX and AVX-512 support assisted CPU-based model inference, executing small model prompt processing at 3,624.52 tokens per second and medium 7B model text generation at 28.25 tokens per second.

The absence of integrated local storage eliminates expenditure on unneeded local NVMe drives, providing resource efficiency for systems that rely on managed network disks such as Azure Premium Storage. The combination of 64 high-frequency vCPUs, 256 GB of memory, and high throughput makes this server well configured for high-traffic web serving, Redis in-memory key-value databases, multi-threaded batch operations, and quantized CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: The Microsoft Azure D64ns_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine delivering 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 256.0 GB of RAM, powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 260 MB L3 cache across 32 physical cores. It features hardware extensions including AVX-512, Intel AMX, and accelerated cryptographic instructions. The server includes no GPUs and no local disk storage, depending entirely on network-attached storage. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier static web serving throughput at 90.06 GB/s and strong Redis performance reaching 71.06 million operations per second. PassMark CPU results are strong at 67,051.45, supported by high cached memory bandwidth and capable CPU-based inference throughput. Conversely, PassMark memory scores and large-block memory transfers remain in lower to average ranges. The instance provides resource density without the cost of unused local storage, making it suitable for high-throughput web serving, Redis caching, database workloads, and CPU-bound model inference.
